sources.note: Nothing. Ch.1 sec.4 'Bhili va Bhilali boli ka udbhav evam svarup' is a folkloristic note with a Bhili/Bhilali/Bareli/Hindi word chart; no phonology, no balaghat/svaraghat discussion.

sources.citation: Varkey, Vinod Wilson & Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Study of Bareli/Pauri and Related Languages. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-011. Dallas: SIL International. 197 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (lexical similarity, RTT, bilingualism); nine Bhilali 210-item IPA wordlists in Appendix C carry no stress marks ('field transcriptions.. have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis', p.74). Useful identity facts: Rathia/Urppa Bhilalas 'speak like the Rathwa Barelas'; Parya Bhilali closer to Nimadi; Sulya 1979's author is a Barela from Khargone.

sources.citation: Phillips, Maxwell P. 2012. Dialect Continuum in the Bhil Tribal Belt: Grammatical Aspects. PhD thesis, SOAS, University of London. 193 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing on stress anywhere (only segmental Wagdi phonology, sec. 3.1); Bhilali is not treated at all. Examined because it is the main modern academic work on the Bhil continuum.

sources.citation: Vunnamatla, Kishore Kumar, Mathews John & Nelson Samuvel. 2012. The Nimadi-speaking people of Madhya Pradesh: A sociolinguistic profile. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-002. Dallas: SIL International. 176 pp.

sources.note: Nothing. Contains a Parya Bhilali (Bhorwada, Barwani) wordlist and RTT results only; no suprasegmental information.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part III: The Bhil languages. Calcutta. Sections 'Bhili of Ali Rajpur' (pp. 61-66) and 'Bhilali of Barwani' / 'Rathvi Bhilali' (pp. 67-68).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Pronunciation notes only (broad o for short a, palatals as in W. Hindi, v>b, cerebral l ~ l/n); Barwani Bhilali 'essentially identical with the dialect spoken in Ali Rajpur.. do not call for any separate remarks'. The only 'accent' hit in the volume is the transcription convention in the front matter.
